questions.question: What is the difference between the spread operator and rest parameters?
questions.title: Spread And Rest
questions.direct_answer: Same syntax (...), opposite directions. SPREAD expands a collection INTO elements — `[...arr1, x]`, `f(...args)`, `{...obj, extra}` — for copying, merging, and calling with an array's contents. REST collects MULTIPLE elements INTO one array — `function f(...items)` (all remaining args), `const [head, ...tail] = arr` (remaining items) — for variadic functions and destructuring remainders. Spread: one → many. Rest: many → one.

    end

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Spread is shallow everywhere (the depth marker that catches seniors too): `[...nested]` copies the array but nested objects/arrays are SHARED references — push into the clone's inner array and the original sees it. Same for objects: `{...obj}` shares nested values. Deep copies need structuredClone(obj) (the modern built-in, handles cycles, no functions) or a JSON round-trip (loses Dates, undefined, functions, Infinity; breaks on cycles) or a library (immer's produce, lodash's cloneDeep).

The iteration contracts (the machinery): spread in array/function contexts consumes the ITERATOR protocol — which is why you can spread strings ([...'abc']), Sets, Maps (entries), and generators, and why spreading a non-iterable throws ({} spread in array context is a TypeError; object spread is different — it uses OwnPropertyKeys, which is why {...arr} gives {0:…, 1:…} — the array's indices become keys).

The newest additions (the 2022+ layer): `Object.groupBy`/`Map.groupBy`, at()/with()/toSorted()/toReversed()/toSpliced() — the immutable-replacement methods — are the ecosystem's push toward the same copy-don't-mutate discipline that made spread the default idiom. The React connection that ties it together: `{...rest}` prop-forwarding (rest-destructure the consumed props, spread the rest onto the wrapped element) and the state-update idiom (`setUser({...user, name: 'x'})`) are the two most-used React patterns built on spread/rest — knowing that connection is what makes this question interview-relevant rather than academic.
